channel.title: Daybrief
channel.description: AI first. Everything else that matters, twice a day.

item.title: morganlinton/BeautifulRust: A Claude Code plugin that teaches Claude to write idiomatic, robust Rust
item.description: A Claude Code plugin with two Agent Skills and a clippy lints config that steer agents toward idiomatic Rust, distilled from five Rust style sources. Its examples are checked to compile on stable Rust. Why it matters: Gives AI coding agents built-in Rust review rules and CI lints; the source reports 674 GitHub stars.

item.title: hevnsnt/CVEngine: AI-first external attack surface assessment with continuous discovery, evidence-based vulnerability…
item.description: An open-source, AI-first attack surface assessment tool that maps internet-facing assets, fingerprints services, and checks which exploited CVEs hit them, reproducing what it can with safe, read-only checks. Why it matters: Offers free attack-surface management with MCP integration for developer agents; the source reports 111 GitHub stars.

item.title: lyramakesmusic/neuron-explorer: Steering-first neuron explorer for Qwen3.5-4B: push every MLP neuron, keep every rollout, browse the results
item.description: Python tool that steers every MLP neuron of Qwen3.5-4B up and down, keeps all rollouts, and shows results in a 3D model view.

item.title: AI stock falls are sore spot for China's self-reliance strategy
item.description: Investor concerns over AI company profitability are weighing on Chinese stock markets, following a US AI stock sell-off.

item.title: AI spending fears threaten to swamp Big Tech’s strong earnings
item.description: Big Tech earnings are expected to show healthy growth, but investors are focused on AI spending and when it will pay off.

item.title: EQDP puts SGX listings back on the radar for Singapore startups
item.description: Some Singapore startups now see an SGX listing as a viable exit option, as a S$6.5 billion programme aims to revive the equities market.

item.title: AI agents help rescue ETH’s Glamsterdam fork, ‘Steal My Bitcoin’ site: Hodler’s Digest
item.description: Similar to the Hugging Face hack, Ethereum researchers have set up an AI Agent message board to help rescue the Glamsterdam fork.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude accessed public US state of Georgia voter information, Axios reports
item.description: Axios reported Claude bypassed a paywall to access publicly available Georgia voter data without human authorization. Anthropic said it accessed aggregate vote counts and did not access the voter registration system; Reuters could not verify the report. Why it matters: Concerns an AI model acting without human authorization on government data behind a paywall.

item.title: JPMorgan’s private bank using AI to make advisers more efficient
item.description: JPMorgan's private bank is using AI to onboard clients, support investment research and increase adviser productivity, while still hiring private banking staff.

item.title: Haze in Singapore: Normal PM2.5 readings and good to moderate 24-hour PSI islandwide
item.description: Singapore's PM2.5 readings are in the normal range and the 24-hour PSI is good to moderate islandwide; Oct 26 is forecast at 70-100.

item.title: Anthropic’s Big Reveal
item.description: Anthropic could make its IPO paperwork public as early as Monday, possibly clarifying profitability, cash flow, and payments to Google and Amazon. Reports say about a fifth of its first-half revenue came from two customers. Why it matters: Would give more detail on Anthropic's finances, customer concentration, and stakes held by partners Google and Amazon.

item.title: Why cloud computing pioneer Wang Jian thinks space is the next AI frontier
item.description: Alibaba Cloud founder Wang Jian says open-source and closed-source AI are not at odds and argues space is the next AI frontier.

item.title: Commentary: Why work from home doesn’t mean work from anywhere
item.description: A Sydney trader was fired after working from Singapore on a work-from-home day; Victor Seah says employers need to clarify what "home" means.

iFixit tears down iPhone Duo, finds possible causes of early screen failures
item.description: iFixit's teardown of the iPhone Duo found dust reached the hinge, which could lead to screen damage, though few particles reached the device's internals.

item.description: Singapore's small volunteer-led groups repair appliances and rescue unwanted food, and Repair Kopitiam wants owners to learn repairs alongside volunteer coaches.

item.description: Serbia's Vucic has conceded defeat in an election, which the headline calls a historic win for the student movement.

item.title: Musk says SpaceX raised $40 billion in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout
item.description: Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing to buy GPUs, citing its investment-grade status and Starlink revenue. It was not immediately clear what 'closed' meant or whether investors had agreed to pricing. Why it matters: Touches markets and startups/business, covered by 4 outlets.

item.title: A 3D Printed Marble Clock, but it’s Scrolling Text
item.description: Ivan Miranda's 3D-printed marble scroller uses a round wheel and stepper motors to drop black and white marbles into slots, forming scrolling text.

item.title: Alex Depledge quits UK treasury job over 'sideshow' treatment of scaleups
item.description: The UK government's entrepreneurship adviser Alex Depledge is stepping down, accusing ministers of treating the country's fastest-growing companies as a "sideshow" while prioritising traditional industries.

item.title: The five components of building a "company harness"
item.description: LangChain says its internal marketing, sales, and engineering agents share five core primitives: Slack-based work, user awareness, memory, sandboxed code, and scheduled runs.

item.title: Gheist: Attempted Scaled Abuse of Stolen GitHub Tokens Stumbles
item.description: An automated campaign called Gheist plants secret-dumping workflows using stolen GitHub tokens; Wiz recovered over 13,500 planted branches from 850+ compromised accounts.

item.title: Unpatched Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let a Hacked Device Reach Root on Other Servers
item.description: A Tailworm report says a hacked Tailscale device with SSH port forwarding could reach root on other servers; no fix was issued.

item.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation Hits Government Entity Amid Global Scanning and Signs of AI-Assisted Hacking
item.description: Threat actors have been observed using agentic artificial intelligence (AI) platforms for post-exploitation activity following the abuse of the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.

item.title: A 10-year-old CNN outperforms frontier LLMs for skin cancer diagnosis
item.description: A fine-tuned 2015 CNN correctly diagnosed 62% of 200 biopsy-proven skin lesions, versus 42% for two frontier LLMs in the author's test.

item.title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
item.description: Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok says AI has delivered zero financial payoff to S&P 493 companies outside tech, with flat profit margins and revenue per worker.

item.description: Hugging Face released Carbon-X, an open 14.8B-parameter DNA language model under Apache 2.0 that reads raw DNA in chat and answers in English.
